content:
Decision to agree
school term and holiday dates for Leicester City maintained schools
for 2027 to 2032.
 

To approve Option 2 outlined in the report as
the agreed model for determining school holiday and term dates for
2027/28 to 2031/32.

Based on consultation
feedback we have listened to parents and stakeholders and agreed
that the updated model 2 provides the best balance based on
responses and feedback.

academic year after the August Bank Holiday, like County
consultation start dates. Agreed to a 1 week Autumn half term
holiday moved to the 3rd week of the month. Maintained the summer
end of term within the 2nd week of July. Want to give schools and
parents confirmation of term dates as early as possible.

– Approve 1 week Autumn Term Model.

decision_maker: Deputy City Mayor - Housing, Economy, and Neighbourhoods
content:
To approve Leicester
City Council working in partnership with Leicestershire County
Council and Rutland County Council to prepare a joint Minerals and
Waste Local Plan across the geographical area of Leicester,
Leicestershire and Rutland, subject to their formal agreement.

Preparing a joint
minerals & waste local plan with Leicestershire County and
Rutland County would be more beneficial than preparing one covering
only the Leicester City Council administrative area, as a joint
plan would enable the pooling of resources between the three
participating authorities, minerals and waste plans are better
suited to covering a greater-than-local scale due to the strategic
nature of minerals and waste planning, and there are very limited
opportunities for locating minerals and waste uses within the city
council’s administrative area.

To prepare a joint
minerals and waste local plan in partnership with Leicestershire
County Council and Rutland County Council, which would cover the
geographical area of the three participating authorities, and which
would be prepared in collaboration by officers of the three
authorities.
 
The other option
considered was to prepare a minerals and waste local plan covering
only the Leicester City Council administrative area and which would
be prepared solely by Leicester City Council planning officers.
topline: The Deputy City Mayor - Housing, Economy, and Neighbourhoods has decided to approve the preparation of a joint Minerals and Waste Local Plan with Leicestershire County Council and Rutland County Council.

content:
To approve disposal of
the ground lease interest of Holiday Inn, St Nicholas Circle
Leicester, LE1 5LX, (UPRN 1427) by way of 1:1 negotiation with the
holder of the ground lease-to the hotel operator (MCAP Global
Finance (UK) LLP) for £1.8m, plus and agreed contribution of
£20,000 for City Council professional fees
 
The Director of
Estates and Building Services has approved the valuation of the
site supported by an external RICS Red Book valuation.
 
It is noted that the
City Barrister and Head of Standards Division will prepare and
execute all necessary documentation required. The Director of
Estates and Building Services Division will agree the required
detailed terms.
 

The sale will enable
Holiday Inn to upgrade and enhance the facility.  The sale will also give a capital sum to the City
Council that exceeds the income stream under the ground lease for
the remainder of the ground lease term. 
It is to be noted that the value of an interest such as this will
decline over time.


i)         
The only option other than accepting the offer made is to continue
with the current ground lease for the remainder of the
term.  This would lead to an overall
lower receipt.

ii)         For the
avoidance of doubt, the interest is unlikely to be saleable at a
beneficial figure other than to the interested party, who is a
Special Purchaser. Sale to any other party would realise less than
the current value of the City Council interest.
 
It is therefore
recommended to proceed with a one-to-one disposal to  MCAP Global Finance
(UK) LLP, for £1.8m as Special Purchaser.
topline: The City Mayor has decided to approve the disposal of the ground lease interest of Holiday Inn in Leicester for £1.8m.

The freehold disposal
of site (UPRN 1983) 52-58 Oxford Street, Leicester, LE1 5XW to

NGED’s
acquisition of the site will enable development as a new primary
substation site that will supply sufficient electrical capacity to
support the infrastructure for the City.
 
The sale will also
generate a capital receipt for the Council of £2m which
represents best consideration.

from NGED to purchase the freehold and continue with the current
existing leases with its annual income or develop the site for
affordable housing.

combined with importance of NGED developing the Strategic Primary
Substation subject to planning.

content:
To approve:
 

•          
A permanent increase of £105,000 to the Arts & Museum
budget ceiling, to support festivals across the City. This will be funded from the budget strategy
reserve in 2026/27 and will be permanently added to the budget
ceiling for Arts & Museums within future budget strategies.

•          
One-off funding of £10k to fund a rebranding of Leicester
Riverside Festival to be funded from the budget strategy
reserve.
 

By investing in
high-quality, inclusive and environmentally responsible festivals
and events, Leicester City Council enables organisations to
co-design and deliver vibrant cultural activity that animates the
city, brings people together, and attracts visitors. This leads to
increased participation, improved wellbeing and pride, stronger
community connections, economic benefit, and a more sustainable,
distinctive cultural identity for Leicester.
 
Recognising the
financial pressures facing many households, the Council is
committed to ensuring that cost is not a barrier to participation
in cultural life. Increased investment will enable more affordable
and accessible opportunities for families, young people and
communities across Leicester to engage with high-quality cultural
experiences, celebrate shared identities and traditions, and
participate in civic life.
 
The increase in the
festivals budget reflects the Council’s commitment to
delivering a more balanced, inclusive and strategically aligned
programme of cultural activity across the city. Additional
investment enables support for a broader range of established,
large-scale, culturally significant and community-led events that
celebrate Leicester’s diversity and heritage, strengthen
community cohesion and civic pride, and create opportunities for
participation across a wide range of communities and age
groups.

To limit funding
support would reduce the ability of the council to support a wide
range of festivals and events that animate the city, promote social
cohesion, enhances wellbeing and civic pride and supports local
businesses and wider economic impact.
topline: The City Mayor has decided to increase funding for arts and museums in Leicester to support festivals and events across the city.

content:
To seek approval to
proceed with the disposal of 344 Harrison Road, Leicester, LE4 7AB
on a one-to-one basis to the neighbouring freeholder AKR Holdings
Ltd., of 336a Harrison Road, Leicester LE4 7AB for £132,500
as a ‘Special Purchaser’ (as defined in the
Council’s Constitution).

To approve the
disposal of 344 Harrison Road, Leicester, LE4 7AB on a one-to-one
basis to the freeholder of 336A Harrison Road, Leicester, LE4 7AB
for £132,500.
 
It is noted that the
City Barrister and Head of Standards Division, will prepare and
execute all necessary documentation required. The Director of
Estates and Building Services Division has agreed the required
detailed terms and valuations.

The subject property
has been vacant for several years and will continue to deteriorate
without extensive refurbishment including structural remediation.
There are party wall implications with the neighbouring property,
344A Harrison Road (owned by the proposed purchaser), and the
property is not suitable for re-letting by the HRA in its current
condition. The HRA wherever possible seeks to acquire property
which is standardised across the portfolio or presents opportunity
for standardisation of layout to support efficiencies for HRA
maintenance. Covenants can be put in place to prevent major
development and for the property to be redeveloped for habitable
occupation within 24 months of completion.


i)         
Disposal on the open market via auction was discounted in favour of
the above market value offer in light of the poor condition of the
property and party wall implications.
 

ii)         The
recommend option is to dispose of the property to the adjacent
freeholder and reinvest the capital receipt into more suitable HRA
stock.
topline: The City Mayor has decided to proceed with the disposal of a deteriorating property at 344 Harrison Road, Leicester, to the neighbouring freeholder AKR Holdings Ltd. for £132,500.

content:
That the Deputy Mayor
for Housing confirm whether the recommendations of the LGSCO will
be complied with in full, and if not, to provide reasons for
declining to comply with any recommendations.

To decline to comply
with one of the four recommendations of the LGSCO - regarding
payment of compensation to Ms X

The recommendation set
out at and 4.4 of the Decision Report are not to be complied with
for the following reasons:
 

•          
The issue that is the subject of the recommendation at 4.4 are not
of the Council’s making. The Regulations regarding
“unsuitability” were made by Parliament in 2003, over
20 years ago. The geopolitical context has changed unrecognisably
since then. Between 2015 and 2025 the numbers presenting to the
city council as homeless increased from 2163 to 6,891 and our
provision, on which we spent over £5million per year, was
overwhelmed, as was the case in comparable cities throughout the
UK. Therefore these pressures a product of forces beyond one
Council’s control, together with policy made by multiple
Government agencies including the Home Office. To seek to penalise
a Council for a national and international crisis is grossly unfair
to the Council and the taxpayers of Leicester.
 

•          
It is impossible to see that the LGSCO have not set a clear
precedent here that they will be bound to follow in other
complaints. This is the second consecutive case in which a
four-figure sum of compensation has been recommended by the
Ombudsman. We calculate this exposure to be £250k for
Leicester City Council, and many millions of pounds nationally.
This could bring Councils closer to the prospect of an unbalanced
General Fund leading to significant and detrimental loss of local
services for local people.
 

•          
The principle of awarding a remedy is predicated upon the public
body who is at fault being able to put-right that error. This is
not the case here. There will be no salutary effect from this
compensatory exposure, because we (like just about every other
Council in the country) have no power to immediately create extra
housing that would avert the need to keep families in B&B for
more than six weeks. The LGSCO recognises that the Council had
nowhere else to place Mr X’s family during this period.
 

•          
We are spending many millions of pounds to respond in a structured
way to the pressures. In the last 12 months the Council has spent
£45m in the acquisition of 253 self-contained family and
single temporary accommodation units. It has also spent over
£400m in conjunction with partners to deliver over 1,800 new
permanent affordable homes in the city, with a further 800 in train
to be delivered by 2027. Exposing us to paying hundreds of
thousands of pounds of compensation will only serve to
significantly set-back our plans to strategically address it. By
investing in new temporary and permanent housing stock we have
reduced the number of families staying in B&Bs from 421 in 2024
to 55 today

1.        
Compliance with all four recommendations
2.        
Compliance with three of the four recommendations
topline: The Deputy City Mayor has decided to decline to comply with the LGSCO recommendation for payment of compensation to Ms X, citing financial constraints and the unfairness of penalizing the council for a crisis beyond its control.
